messages:
oliver: Quick RFC follow-up idea — sketching a lightweight soft-fallback negotiation between frontdoor and upstreams. Goal: let gateway advertise 'fallback semantics' early so edge can degrade midstream without user-visible dupes. Thoughts?

anya: short version: add a header that encodes safe-fallback options? e.g. X-RW-Fallback: variant=smaller,consistency=best_effort,side_effects=unsafe

sam: hm. midstream downgrade for streaming responses is hairy. how do we ensure dedupe / idempotency if upstream switches model?

jules: two parts: 1) routing hint header to choose eligible fallbacks before request start 2) a small runtime token that we can attach to streaming chunks so downstream can detect a fallback boundary.

leo: sketch of headers: 
- X-RW-Fallback-Policy: prefer-quantized|prefer-latency|prefer-cost
- X-RW-Fallback-Token: base64(<request-id>:<seed>)
would let proxies know which downstreams are acceptable and mark streams with token when fallback occurs.

oliver: exactly. and we can define token semantics to mean 'safe to stitch with previous chunks if token matches' — otherwise gateway must abort and return truncated final. That keeps client-visible consistency.

sam: concern: that leaks routing intent and tenant preferences to upstreams. also multi-tenant environments might not want that policy visible. need opt-in and masking.

anya: we can scope headers to internal hops only (edge -> control-plane -> compute). strip at egress to customer. also only set when tenant config allows soft-fallback.

jules: another tradeoff: backpressure & memory. If edge keeps both original stream and fallback warm to switch without losing tokens, that's memory heavy. alternative: accept a short seamless window where we replay last N tokens from client to fallback backend. but that requires upstream determinism.

leo: replay is feasible for stateless generation (prompt+seed). For cached KV state (kvcache) it fails. maybe prefer a quick checkpoint handshake: when fallback requested, upstream responds with a short checkpoint trailer: `FALLBACK_CHECKPOINT: offset=482` which proxy can use to resume.

sam: trailers for a streaming path feels risky — many clients and browsers don't surface trailers. This is internal-only though, right?

oliver: yes internal-only. we use trailers on internal HTTP/2/grpc between frontdoor and compute. clients see only final response or an abort with a clear semantic.

anya: telemetry: important to tag metrics as 'soft_fallback_attempt' and 'fallback_success' to tune thresholds. Also log the chosen policy for chargeback.

jules: also need SLO semantics: if fallback incurs higher hallucination risk, product teams must opt in. we should make quality downgrade explicit in response metadata (x-rw-quality-change: probability_estimate=0.12) so app layers can react.

leo: implementation note: router should validate fallback chain compatibility (model arch, tokenizer). if incompatible, we should either not nominate that fallback or mark as 'requires-rescore' and fail closed.

sam: open question: how do we charge? if we switch midstream to a cheaper model, billing attribution should split by tokens produced by each backend. need token-level accounting in gateway.

oliver: agreed — gateway will emit per-chunk provenance (internal only) like `{token_index,start_ts,backend_id}` into metrics/eventstream. that'll be used for billing reconciliation.

anya: operational: add a kill-switch config per-tenant to disable midstream switch. and a safety heuristic: only allow fallback within first X tokens or after an idempotent guard.

jules: one more: tests — we should add a chaos test that simulates upstream capacity drop midstream and verifies client-visible semantics (no duplication, no silent content loss beyond acceptable truncation).

oliver: next steps: I'll draft a minimal header + trailer spec and a short checklist for implementation (router validation, tokenization compatibility check, telemetry events, tenant opt-in). Who wants to review the PR?

sam: me.

anya: me as well.

jules: happy to review the tests.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: Scheduled rollout checkpoint: feature/soft-fallback will be gated behind `edge.soft_fallback` flag in staging starting 2026-03-12.

leo: thanks — I'll add billing events to the chargeback pipeline and a draft quip in docs.

oliver: great, thanks everyone. I'll post the spec link once it's up and tag reviewers. :thumbsup:
